summary: Streaming race after auth token refresh causes interleaved paragraphs and missing closing punctuation
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that long-running SSE streams intermittently return interleaved paragraph fragments and sometimes omit final punctuation after a short auth token rotation. Impact: QuantaDocs observed 3-7% of streaming responses missing closing punctuation or containing sentences where paragraphs are mixed (two paragraphs merged with parts out of order). This leads to downstream parsing failures for their document ingestion pipeline. Environment: Production, us-east-1, Dedicated tenancy with token rotation frequency: 5 minutes for short-lived session tokens. Steps to reproduce (observed by customer): 1) Start an SSE chat session to /v1/streams with a standard system+user prompt that elicits a multi-paragraph long-form answer (~300-500 tokens). 2) Allow the session to be open for >3 minutes. 3) Trigger an auth refresh (customer-side or via normal rotate) or wait for automatic token refresh to happen. 4) Client reconnects/resumes using the session id/last-event-id; sometimes receives interleaved fragments from two worker backends. Expected: Resume should stitch fragments in order and preserve terminal punctuation. Actual: On ~3-7% of attempts, the resumed stream contains chunks that interleave paragraph fragments (e.g., the end of paragraph 1 followed by the beginning of paragraph 3, then the remainder of paragraph 2), and in ~1% the closing punctuation for the final paragraph is missing. Additional notes: Customer uses an HTTP reverse proxy before the client which preserves Last-Event-ID header. They rely on the server-provided resume token in SSE body. They experimented with longer token TTL and saw reduced frequency.
steps_to_reproduce: Open SSE stream to /v1/streams with a prompt returning multi-paragraph output (~400 tokens)
Keep the connection idle for >3 minutes so token rotation will occur on client or server side
Allow auth-flow to issue a new short-lived token, then perform reconnect/resume using Last-Event-ID or resume token
Observe assembled stream for out-of-order paragraph fragments and missing final punctuation

investigation_notes: Initial support triage: reproduced at low rate on staging when forcing short token TTL to 10s and performing reconnect during mid-generation.

Hypothesis 1: resume routing race — resume request can be routed to a different worker which begins producing the next sequence before the previous worker finishes sending its tail; mismatch in sequence ordering in assembly logic causes interleaving.
Hypothesis 2: token rotation causes a transient double-connection window where both workers consider themselves authoritative for the session; last-event-id hints diverge between workers.

Observed evidence: logs show overlapping seq numbers and two workers (worker-08 and worker-12) with partial_choice_ids pc_43 and pc_44 both sending segments within milliseconds of each other. Assembly reported "mismatch" and sequence array indicates out-of-order arrival: [202,203,201].

Edge-proxy behavior: proxy preserves Last-Event-ID header, but when cookie/token rotates, client may open a new TCP connection that LB routes to a different backend; LB sticky session TTL observed to be 30s so not always sticky across rotates.

Reproducer: integration test created that simulates rotation mid-stream and triggers reconnect; failing rate ~5/1000 on local agent with two simulated workers; increasing inter-worker arbitration (locking) reduced failure rate to zero in the test harness.

Potential regressions: recent change in resume orchestration (PR #2387) touched worker handoff and reduce-lock path for resume speed — may have opened a microwindow where two workers can both believe they should serve the resumed stream.

resolution: Workaround: customer set reverse-proxy affinity for 30s and temporarily increased token TTL to 10 minutes (reduced failures to <0.1%). Permanent fix: serving-runtime patch #2399 (adds short resume lease + stricter sequence handshake) merged and scheduled for staged rollout. Follow-ups: 1) QA regression for resume fast-path to add synthetic test forcing mid-generation rotate; 2) Monitor canary metrics for interleaving events in us-east-1; 3) Update runbook with guidance for customers using short-lived auth tokens during long-lived SSE streams. Ticket remains open until canary completes and customer confirms resolution.
